items.lesson: One-sided retrieval causing absence-based comparison errors is inconclusive: the pre-final deferral faithfully issued the second-entity search, but the corpus returned no title-count evidence (data sufficiency failed), so trial_004's repeated absence-based conclusion is a data/environment confound, not mechanism attribution. Do not rely unchanged; a revisit requires retrieval/corpus supplying the second-entity evidence or a success condition independent of absent passages.
items.applicability: Absence-based comparison errors in one-sided retrieval tasks where the second entity's evidence is absent from returned passages; scope is this data-limited setting, released when data sufficiency for the required evidence is confirmed.

items.lesson: One-sided-retrieval causing absence-based comparison errors is inconclusive: trial_004 faithfully fired the required second-entity search (implementation confirmed) yet returned passages lacked Cia Berg title-count evidence, so the repeated absence-based conclusion is a data-sufficiency confound, not an attributed retrieval effect. Stop unchanged and revisit only when the corpus returns the second-entity evidence the success condition requires.
items.applicability: Absence-based comparison-error hypotheses tested via pre-final retrieval deferral on corpus-grounded tasks; recheck only when returned passages contain the second-entity evidence required by the success condition, otherwise keep the direction unchanged.

items.lesson: Testing whether one-sided retrieval causes absence-based comparison errors: the one-shot second-entity search deferral was faithfully executed (trial_004 searched Cia Berg), but the corpus returned no title-count evidence, so the causal claim could not be judged; the repeated absence-based conclusion is confounded by missing corpus facts, not confirmatory. Disposition: inconclusive. Revisit only with controlled second-entity evidence coverage.
items.applicability: Applies to absence-based comparison error hypotheses tested via corpus-retrieval deferral, only where second-entity evidence coverage is known or controllable. Does not support Student capability claims.

items.lesson: The claim that inserting generic verification context causes a follow-up search before finalization is falsified: on four faithful positive activations, three finalized without any search, and the only search success also occurred in the untreated source control, with no differential action-type effect. Stop unchanged; revisit only with a mechanism or evidence showing an activation-attributed differential search effect.
items.applicability: Applies only to the mechanism 'inserted verification context induces pre-finalization follow-up search' on faithful positive activations; negative-stratum coverage is excluded as non-causal. Revisit requires activation-attributed differential search vs matched control.

required_concepts: require a differential effect against control

Stop unchanged; revisit only with a treated-versus-control differential follow-up-search effect.

Reject this generic direction unchanged; do not rely on it unchanged to drive gap-based search.
